Subject: Q1 capacity segmentation proposal and temporary exception for AsterBio pilot

Team —

I put together a short proposal (attached) to experiment with capacity segmentation for Q1. The ask is to reserve a small, low-latency pool ("band A") for a short pilot with AsterBio so they can validate a real-time inference flow. Key points:

- Pilot window: 2027-01-03 to 2027-01-31 (4 weeks of traffic)
- Requested reserved capacity: 8 T4-equivalent slots (could be mixed on-disk quantized variants)
- Autoscale exception: allow burst-to-12 slots for bursts during lab demos (max 48 hours consecutive)
- SLO target from customer: p95 < 120ms, sustained throughput ~120 req/s
- Rollback: automatic fallback to standard pool after pilot or on regression

Attachments: capacity_segmentation_v1.xlsx — includes proposed pool bands, cost delta estimate, and an initial monitoring/alerting checklist.

Asking for:
1) Ops sign-off on feasibility and guardrails (Marcus, Dev)
2) PM guidance on config and customer-facing messaging (Kimberly)
3) CS confirmation of the minimum acceptance criteria from AsterBio (Lauren)

If we can agree on guardrails by Dec 3 I can confirm the pilot and capture in the deal terms.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Capacity Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q1 capacity segmentation proposal and temporary exception for AsterBio pilot

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear doc. Quick thoughts:

- The banding idea (A: latency-sensitive, B: standard reserved, C: experimental/burst) makes sense. I want to avoid open-ended exceptions that create long-term precedence.
- For the customer, we should be explicit: this is a time-limited reserved lane with documented fallbacks and no SLA extension beyond the pilot. We can offer a 30% credit if we miss the agreed p95 target more than twice.
- Question on telemetry: will we surface token-level cost and per-route p95 in the same dashboard or a separate pilot dashboard? Marcus/Dev — we need a minimal dashboard spec so CS doesn't have to scramble.

Also, two operational asks from product side:
1) Limit autoscale exception to a defined burst window and require manual approval to extend beyond the 48h caps.
2) Lock the model version for the pilot to avoid accidental pushes into band A.

Happy to discuss Thursday.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q1 capacity segmentation proposal and temporary exception for AsterBio pilot

Agree with Kim. A few operational constraints and a proposed runbook fragment attached.

- Feasibility: we can carve an 8-slot reserved lane. To keep scheduling simple we'll tag with pool:band=A and limit to specific model ids.
- Autoscale: allowing burst to 12 slots for short demo windows is doable but must be controlled via an ops-initiated policy with hard TTLs. We should enforce per-customer quota so bursts can't starve other pilots.
- Monitoring: propose these alerts — p95 > 150ms (warning), p95 > 200ms (critical); Increased queue length > 40ms per-token for 2 consecutive minutes; sudden token-cost > 30% above baseline.

Attachment: ops_runbook_template.md — includes steps to create the lane, enforce model pinning, and rollbacks.

Note: we will need a temporary reservation ticket in the capacity service and a human on-call during initial 72 hours of pilot to watch for noisy neighbors. Ops cost estimate: ~3 engineer-hours/day during first week.

Thanks — operationally fine with the carve as described, with one caveat: autoscale exceptions require a small code change to the scoring/routing layer so we can gate bursts by TTL and by per-customer allowance. I can have a scoped change ready by Dec 14 but it will need a short canary (we can run it in staging and then a single rack for production).

Proposed guardrails:
- Burst TTL: 48 hours cumulative in a 7-day window, enforced by routing layer.
- Manual escalation path: binary flag to disable bursts immediately.
- Canary rollout: 1 rack -> monitor 12 hours -> 3 racks -> monitor 24 hours -> full.

Cost impact: small infra change + 2 engineer-days for canary run + 6 engineer-hours/day ops during week 0.

- AsterBio expects p95 < 120ms for interactive lab work. If we can't meet that threshold they will pause demos.
- They're comfortable with a time-limited lane and understand fallback to standard pool will increase latency.
- They asked for a simple dashboard (p95, error-rate, token-cost) and a single Slack channel to reach ops during demo windows.

Ellen — can you confirm acceptance of the credit construct Kimberly suggested and confirm the busiest demo days? We want to align the burst TTL around their heaviest schedule.

- Approve temporary capacity segmentation for AsterBio pilot (2027-01-03 -> 2027-01-31).
- Reserve 8 slots (band A) with gated burst to 12 slots subject to Dev's TTL enforcement and canary rollout.
- Ops will staff 72 hours after pilot start; Marcus to raise the temporary reservation ticket and assign on-call.
- Product will lock model id and expose the pilot dashboard as a subset of the Redwood Console (Kimberly + Marcus to own).
- CS (Lauren) will confirm demo calendar and Slack channel; Ellen to confirm credit acceptance by Dec 6.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Dev: PR for routing TTL and canary plan by Dec 14. (Dev)
- Marcus: Reservation ticket + runbook + on-call schedule by Dec 10. (Marcus)
- Kimberly: Dashboard spec and customer messaging by Dec 8. (Kimberly)
- Lauren: Customer sign-off (Ellen) and busiest demo dates by Dec 6. (Lauren)

If anyone thinks a longer pilot is necessary we should treat it as a new revenue/contract conversation rather than an ops exception — I want this to stay a short, instrumented experiment.

I'll open the HubSpot deal note and attach the capacity_segmentation_v1.xlsx + ops_runbook_template.md.

Thanks — moving to action.
